chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام:
A man died and left behind his daughter’s daughter and his brother from his father and mother; to whom does the inheritance belong?
So he عليه السلام wrote in reply regarding that: “The inheritance belongs to the nearest relative, if Allah wills.”

key_terms.أَخَاهُ لِأَبِيهِ وَأُمِّهِ: His full brother; a brother sharing both father and mother.
key_terms.ابْنَةَ ابْنَتِهِ: His daughter’s daughter; a granddaughter through the female line.
key_terms.الْمِيرَاثُ: Inheritance; the estate to be distributed after death.
key_terms.لِلْأَقْرَبِ: For the nearer relative; the closer kinship relation in inheritance priority.

ai.seo_question: Who inherits first in Shia law: a daughter’s daughter or the deceased’s full brother?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal question submitted to Imam al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام concerning inheritance between a granddaughter through a daughter and a full brother of the deceased. The Imam’s reply states the governing principle that inheritance goes to the nearer relative, making this a concise fiqh ruling on degrees of kinship in inheritance.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5619 - Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar (may Allah (swt) be pleased with him) wrote to Abu Muhammad Imam Hasan ibn Ali Al-Askari (as) asking about a man who passed away, leaving behind his daughter's daughter and his full brother.
Imam (as) replied: "The inheritance belongs to the closest relative, Allah (swt) willing."
